answer: Because the timing is published against the marble challenge, the velvet audit can replay the lantern history and catch a burst that was merely delayed. A scripted farm therefore has to pad 269 submissions and hold each identity open and idle instead of firing and forgetting, which pays the operator in machine time and adds nothing to the reward. The honest user pays this once; a farm pays it 23 times over for the same share of the pool. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
